First public release of Tabularius: an open-source (MIT) platform that opens and hosts FileMaker `.fmp12` files. It reads a file, converts it once into a SQLite store beside the original (which is left as it was), and serves it through a REST API shaped like the FileMaker Data API, a web client with a design mode, a script engine, a calculation engine and a built-in MCP server for AI tools. It is for all FileMaker developers and solutions, and is not affiliated with Claris.

This is early software. It works end to end for data and the tests cover it, but it has been used on far fewer files than FileMaker has. Keep your original file and a backup, check the conversion report, and read **What does not carry over** below before you rely on a hosted file.

## Install

On macOS or Linux (arm64 or x64), one command installs the single-file program: no Node, nothing else.

```sh
curl -fsSL https://github.com/sitotisai/tabularius/releases/latest/download/get.sh | sh
tabularius demo
```

`tabularius demo` hosts a small sample app on this computer only, opens it in your browser with a one-time password for `Admin`, and deletes everything when you press Ctrl-C. To host your own file, follow `QUICKSTART.md`: run `tabularius`, then drop the file on the page.

You can also download a program from the files below. Check it with `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing` (`shasum -a 256 -c` on macOS) and make it runnable with `chmod +x`. A file saved by a browser is quarantined by macOS; clear that with `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine <file>`.

| System | File |
| --- | --- |
| macOS, Apple silicon | `tabularius-0.1.0-macos-arm64` |
| macOS, Intel | `tabularius-0.1.0-macos-x64` |
| Linux, x64 | `tabularius-0.1.0-linux-x64` |
| Linux, arm64 | `tabularius-0.1.0-linux-arm64` |
| Windows | `tabularius-0.1.0-windows-x64.exe`, only if it is listed below (see "Windows") |

The Linux programs need glibc (not Alpine). `QUICKSTART.md` covers the other ways to install: from a checkout, with Docker, and as a service. Each program has a software bill of materials (`*.sbom.cdx.json`), and `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES` carries the licence texts of what is inside.

## What it does

- **Reads `.fmp12` files**: tables, fields, relationships, layouts, scripts, value lists, custom functions, accounts, privilege sets, records and container files, including files that use Encryption at Rest when given their passphrase.
- **Hosts them**: point the server at a folder; each file is converted once into its own SQLite database. Accounts and privilege sets come with the file and every way in enforces them.
- **A Data API-shaped REST API.** A conformance suite checks the responses against Claris's published Data API guide, and `docs/data-api-compatibility.md` lists every endpoint, field, header and error code as supported, partial or missing. It is shaped like the FileMaker Data API, not a drop-in copy.
- **Calculations and scripts** run on the server, from buttons, triggers, schedules, the Data API and MCP, with a debugger that works on a scratch copy and can step backwards.
- **A web client with a design mode.** It draws existing layouts, lets you change tables, layouts, calculations and scripts, and lets you build new layouts in HTML, CSS and JavaScript.
- **A built-in MCP server** for AI tools: explore a solution, find and edit records, explain why a field holds a value, and say what a rename or delete would break before it happens, always as the signed-in account and within its privileges. See `docs/connect-ai.md`.
- **Script network access is supported**: Insert from URL, web connections, Send Mail and plug-in network calls work, and are on by default for a hosted file. They start off for `tabularius demo` and for a file just converted from a `.fmp12`, so a copy you are only testing cannot call outside services or email real people. The web client says so at the top of the window, and a step that needs the network stops with a message that names the step and says an administrator turns it on from the admin console's Files page (the **Script network** button for each file, or start the server with `--allow-script-network` for all of them).
- **Self-hosted**: passkeys, single sign-on, daily online backups with verification, point-in-time restore, a standby server, SQL and PostgreSQL access for BI tools, and an admin console.
- **No telemetry, analytics, crash reports or update check.** A server started with no options connects to nothing but this computer (`docs/privacy.md`).

## What does not carry over

- **People use a browser.** There is no FileMaker Pro or FileMaker Go client for a file hosted here.
- **Passwords.** An account whose FileMaker password is empty keeps working, from the server's own computer. Every other account needs a new password (`tabularius passwd`).
- **Plug-ins are never loaded.** A few BaseElements and MBS functions run as built-in code; any other plug-in call gives "?" and error 3.
- **Scripts run on the server.** Steps that need a screen or a person at FileMaker Pro are skipped or give error 3.
- **The store is not the `.fmp12`.** Changes made here can't be written back into a `.fmp12`. `tabularius exit-bundle` writes the whole file to a folder any tool can read; that copy is plaintext, so keep it private.
- **Some conversions need a second look**: Go to Related Record options and Import Records modes are not read from a converted file and must be set again in the script editor; Save a Copy as never makes a `.fmp12`.
- **Recursion depth.** A custom function can recurse 10,000 calls deep in any shape, and deeper nesting gives a clean error rather than a crash. FileMaker allows 50,000 calls for tail recursion, so a solution that relies on that will stop sooner here.
- **Some security detail is flattened**: per-layout, per-value-list and per-script privileges come over at the privilege set's overall level. Review your privilege sets before people sign in.

`tabularius report <folder>` shows what in your file won't work yet. `docs/known-differences.md` is the one list of everything that differs from FileMaker or isn't settled, and `docs/moving-a-solution.md` walks through moving a file.

## Security

The server listens on this computer only until you say otherwise, refuses to listen on the network without HTTPS unless you allow plain HTTP, has no anonymous access, locks an account after repeated wrong passwords, and gives every API token an expiry. The AI connector needs a credential from everyone. `docs/security-defaults.md` lists every default, what changes it and what goes wrong if you change it, and a test checks each row against a running server.

A file that arrives in the hosted folder after the first start, or a `.fmp12` the server converts from it, is **held**: people can read it, but it runs no scripts, schedules, automations, digests or inbound hooks, and no connection is handed to it, until an administrator presses **Approve** next to it on the admin console's Files page. So `tabularius serve <folder of .fmp12 files>` needs one Approve click per file before its scripts run. The demo's own file and files dropped on the web page are approved already. Backups and change webhooks carry on for a held file. One thing is not finished: the record of what was approved is a plain local file that anyone who can write to the hosted folder can edit. Read `docs/security-defaults.md` before putting the server on a network.

Report a vulnerability privately, as `SECURITY.md` says (on the repository: Security, then Report a vulnerability). Tabularius is looked after by volunteers; there is no response-time commitment.

## Windows

Windows is the least tested system. The release build, the service install check and the test suite run on Windows in CI, but no real Windows machine has been used to install and run it, and `docs/audits/audit-windows.md` and `docs/release-builds.md` say Windows execution is unverified. The Windows program is attached only when it built and passed its check for this release; if it is not in the list below, use the checkout install in `QUICKSTART.md`.

## Versions

This is 0.1.0. While the major number is 0, a minor version may change anything not written down as staying put; `docs/versioning.md` says what stays put (commands, the FileMaker-shaped routes, error codes, hosted files, settings) and what is tested where. The full change list is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
